question: I want a portable power station that comes with a solar panel for camping. Which kit should I buy?
query: best portable power station solar panel kit for camping 2026 EcoFlow Jackery Bluetti comparison

replays.text:
For most campers, I’d buy the **EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max paired with the 220W solar panel**. It’s the clearest ready-to-go station-and-panel setup in the results, and the guide recommends it for campers who want more capability than a weekend-sized unit. [Portable Power Authority’s review](https://portablepowerauthority.com/post/portable-power-station-with-built-in-solar-panel/)

If you’re mainly charging phones, lights, and smaller gear on weekend trips, the **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** is a lighter-class alternative—but make sure the specific package you buy includes a SolarSaga panel, since panel bundles can vary. [Camping comparison](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)

**My pick for most camping trips: the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 with a SolarSaga panel bundle.** It offers 1,070Wh of capacity at about 23.8 lb—more manageable to transport than the larger multi-day units. It can take up to 400W of solar input, so you can add a second 200W SolarSaga panel later if you want faster recharging. [Camping comparison and specs](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)

When buying, make sure the listing explicitly says the **SolarSaga panel is included**: panel wattage and bundle contents vary by package.

If you want more solar-charging headroom and don’t mind a heavier station, consider the **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus** instead; it supports up to 1,000W solar input and weighs about 28 lb. [Comparison details](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)

**My pick: the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus with a compatible EcoFlow solar panel.** It’s the strongest all-round car-camping option in the comparison: 1,024Wh capacity, 1,800W output, up to 1,000W solar input, and about 28 lb. It can also expand later if your power needs grow. [See the camping comparison](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/).

When you shop, make sure the listing is explicitly a **station-and-panel bundle**: the comparison notes that panel wattage varies by package, and the station may be listed on its own.

If keeping weight down matters more, choose the **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 with a SolarSaga panel** instead. It’s about 23.8 lb, with 1,070Wh capacity and a 400W solar-input limit—an easier carry for weekend camping. ([Comparison and specs](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/))
